D.t: Dan Ahlers trails by 13.9 and wins 4% of simulations. Closing it takes about 26,795 voters switching sides, or 53,590 more net votes from new turnout.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between R +23.0 and R +4.3. Only an unusual polling error changes the winner.

The polls page average is R +18.0. Your best recent poll is Concord Public Opinion Partners (D) at R +12.7; your worst is Mason-Dixon for South Dakota News Watch and USD Chiesman Center at R +19.2. 3 polls in the last 30 days.

The biggest vote banks for Democrats: Minnehaha, a projected net 7,383 votes; Oglala Lakota, a projected net 2,778 votes; Clay, a projected net 1,636 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: Minnehaha, D +8.9, 21.7% of the vote; Pennington, R +10.4, 13.1% of the vote; Lincoln, R +9.3, 8.2% of the vote; Brown, R +9.6, 4.0% of the vote.

D.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
D.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, Dan Ahlers runs furthest behind in Butte, Hughes, Meade. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: White voters, 91% of voters, 40 to 58, where a 5 point gain is worth 4.56 points; Voters who cast ballots in 2022 and 2024, 74% of voters, 40 to 58, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.69 points; Voters without a degree, 64% of voters, 40 to 57, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.19 points.

The forecast's worst groups for Dan Ahlers: Immigration voters 16 to 82, Voters who can afford daily costs 32 to 66, Incomes $125K and up 36 to 62. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
